_comment: Askari Bank (AKBL), written against real messages.
Loads after 10-wallets.json and before 20-banks.json, so these claim an
Askari message before the broad sender-recognition rule does.
The recurring difficulty in this bank's wording is that an incoming
transfer names two parties: the sender, and the account holder receiving
it. A naive 'received from (.+)' swallows both. Each pattern below stops
the merchant at whichever comes first - the counterparty's account marker
('AKBL A C *0462') or the ' in ' that introduces the recipient.
An outgoing RAAST transfer has the same two parties in the opposite
order: the payee first, the user's own account second. So the masked id
nearest the start of the message is precisely the one that must NOT
become last4, and askari-transfer-debit anchors last4 to
'from your ... A/C' instead. Left to the generic extractor, that message
returned the payee's RAAST ID as the account the money left.
